title: Attribute slow first boot of the fixed systemd VM
objective: Use bounded owner-authorized measurements to identify the source of the 480.334s first VM start/readiness interval without changing production deadlines or provisioning semantics speculatively.

acceptance_criteria.text: A source-level trace maps first-boot provisioning, guest cloud-init, package/network operations, systemd dependencies, SSH retries, and readiness predicates with exact evidence references.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Delegated read-only trace recorded in ticket tests.created with exact references: systemd/little-mester-vm.service:18-25; lib/vm/system-vm.py:388-406,630-663; lib/vm/guest-bootstrap.py:16-60,118-132; lib/vm/parent-session-contract.py:122-145; systemd/little-mester-vm-proxy.service:3-5; original feat/vm-approach lib/vm/cloud-init.sh; transient CI tests/ci-kvm-stage.sh:579-605,693-744. Conclusion: initial 480.334s interval cause remains unknown; plausible cloud-init package work versus host network-online/proxy, SSH retry and protected readiness alternatives.

acceptance_criteria.text: An owner-authorized hosted run captures enough bounded timestamps/log markers to distinguish host-unit startup, QEMU/guest boot, cloud-init/package work, SSH transport, and protected readiness checks; secrets are excluded.

The measured cause and uncertainty are recorded; any proposed behavior change receives separate Sol design review and preserves deadlines, fresh-provision acceptance, security, and coverage unless an owner-approved evidence-based change says otherwise.
If no actionable defect or unnecessary delay is demonstrated, document the result and leave performance optimization deferred without speculative changes.

These are relative resolver plans, not exact fresh-guest package counts. CI run 45155780845 source SHA 710bbf67f52a11826a3e7bc2e5da8f1c8b9923cf: production systemd job 137628207635 failed while guest APT was still at Ubuntu repository-index Get:29 after 15 minutes per owner-provided excerpt; raw job logs return 403, and exact request timing/layer is unavailable. Host APT's 14-second update is not comparable because it bypasses the guest QEMU guestfwd/socat -> host proxy route. Source shows prior proxy serial 20-second per-address dialing, per-request Connection: close/no reuse, and 60-second relay idle timeout; these make repeated gaps plausible but do not establish the CI root cause. A bounded staggered 20-second-total dial plus redacted phase diagnostics was implemented as a source-level resilience measure; tests/vm-proxy.test.py 22 passed, but there is no hosted evidence of improved APT completion. The transient CI timing/progress changes are not production measurement and do not satisfy owner-authorized production timing acceptance.

Follow-up local regression after review: proxy limits each pending candidate to 3s, advances through later same-family DNS answers while retaining max two active and a 20s overall dial deadline; loser status exceptions do not discard another ready connection; upstream EOF-before-response has a truthful summary. Transient guest-stage failure paths were made single-report under the actual ERR trap. Final local focused results: proxy 24, transient unit 108, stage-state 6, QEMU-owner 7; shell/Python/workflow/diff checks pass. This is not production timing or hosted APT acceptance; exact-commit Sol re-review is pending.

Read-only trace of lib/vm/proxy.py timing: request_ms includes destination policy/DNS/connect plus request send, origin wait and client relay; direct-path upstream_ms starts after connect but before request send and is emitted after client sendall. It can distinguish pre-connect from post-connect time, not request-send, origin TTFB and downstream-relay components. Local regression confirms upstream HTTP 520 status bytes are forwarded unchanged; no live destination/provider attribution.

Deterministic tests/vm-proxy.test.py coverage: client half-close response relay, unchanged upstream 520, pre-response EOF 502 and idle-timeout 502; 26 tests pass. This validates local behavior only, not first-boot timing or hosted APT.
cases: Owner reports run 44947379075 first initial VM start/readiness 480.334s, same-disk restart/readiness 18.275s, fresh provisioning 15.945s, candidate install 1.473s, forced-stop recovery 35.717s, final cleanup 18.733s, TUI 2.754s. Timings localize the delay to first start/readiness but do not attribute it.

Delegated source trace found cloud-init readiness waits for guest runcmd, which includes two apt updates/package installs, Docker repository/package setup, rootless Docker configuration and global npm OpenCode install. Host proxy/network-online dependencies and SSH polling remain possible contributors. No actual first-boot bug established; no timing bounds changed.

Source investigation distinguishes a first-only plausible cloud-init runcmd cost (apt/base packages, Docker repo and second apt, Docker packages, rootless setup, npm OpenCode) from possible host network-online/proxy delay, SSH poll time and protected readiness checks. No per-command guest timestamps exist; 480.334s first readiness cannot be attributed from current evidence. Same-disk 18.275s restart does not prove initial cause. Original bootstrap is materially similar; transient CI is smaller/non-comparable. No proven bug or justified timeout/coverage modification.

Sol APPROVED the consolidated acceptance gap analysis and owner runbook only. First-boot classification is accepted as cause UNKNOWN; measure on a genuinely fresh, separately owner-authorized disposable target with bounded host unit/QEMU/cloud-init/apt-dpkg/SSH-readiness timestamps. A same-disk rerun may not reproduce cloud-init first-boot costs. No action is authorized on either existing owner VM. If later evidence identifies a defect, obtain a separate Sol design review before implementation.

Evidence supports Ubuntu's npm APT package as a top-level source of the large split node-* / node-gyp tree; recommendations also account for compiler/docs packages. Shared bootstrap replaces only the npm APT package, retains unversioned Node, libnode-dev and build-essential, keeps rootless prerequisite recommendations, and leaves proxy/QEMU isolation and the 16-minute service bound unchanged. This is evidence for reducing package work, not proof that upstream network latency was not an additional cause or that the hosted readiness bound now passes. User-provided attempts 1/2 show hundreds of package downloads; attempt 3 step failed after 16 minutes and detailed log archive was unavailable (403).
